title: Growing a Tree Through the Clutter: RRT and RRT-Connect for an Arm, Why Two Trees Beat One, and the Planner That Must Know When to Give Up

artifact.note: sampling based planning for an arm in joint space: a random sample inside the joint limits (the goal itself some of the time), the nearest node of a tree, a step towards the sample of at most a set length, the edge checked by conservative advancement (30-02) and the node kept if it is free; RRT, which grows one tree from the start until a node can be joined to the goal; RRT-Connect, which grows a tree from each end and tries to join the new node to the other tree, swapping the trees; a path read back through the parents; and a planner that gives up after a number of iterations or at once if an end is in collision
